Here are the findings based on Tesla's most recent 10-K filing (filed **January 29, 2026**):

---

### 📊 Tesla, Inc. (TSLA) — Annual Revenue

| Fiscal Year | Period End | Revenue |
|---|---|---|
| FY 2025 | Dec 31, 2025 | $94.83 billion |
| FY 2024 | Dec 31, 2024 | $97.69 billion |

---

### 📉 Year-over-Year Change

$$\frac{94.83 - 97.69}{97.69} \times 100 = \mathbf{-2.93\%}$$

**Tesla's revenue declined by approximately 2.9%** in its latest fiscal year (FY2025), falling from **$97.69 billion** to **$94.83 billion** — a decrease of roughly **$2.86 billion**.

> ⚠️ **Educational note:** A revenue dip of this magnitude for a growth company like Tesla is notable. Factors that can drive such changes include pricing strategy (Tesla made several price cuts in recent years), delivery volumes, macroeconomic pressures, and competitive dynamics. For a deeper understanding of management's explanation, Tesla's 10-K filing would be the primary source to consult.
